rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.001, tv_lambda_init=0.2, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-9 (breast_ct). CLIMB the lambda axis (the productive lever, FOUND). iter-8 BREAKTHROUGH: tv_lambda_init 1e-3->0.05 gave hr=0.1195 (psnr 37.43>baseline 36.32, ssim 0.951>0.920) -- FIRST above-baseline. MECHANISM (diagnosed): step[k] still collapses to ~1.8e-6, but the optimiser GROWS lambda from 0.05 to ~0.30 across epochs so the product step*lambda*tv_grad stays non-zero and denoises the FBP sparse-view noise. So LAMBDA, not step, is the escape from the FBP attractor. iter-8 ended with lambda ~0.30, well above its 0.05 init -> the init was below the productive operating point. ONE KNOB: tv_lambda_init 0.05->0.2 (closer to where iter-8's lambda settled; step_init=1e-3, K=10, mse, per-iter, lr=5e-3). HYPOTHESIS: initialising lambda near its learned operating point (0.2) lets the 10-epoch budget spend more steps in the productive denoising regime rather than climbing from 0.05, so hr rises above 0.1195. FALSIFIER: if hr drops (0.2 over-smooths breast fine structure) the optimum lambda_init is between 0.05 and 0.2 and iter-10 bisects. BUDGET: K=10 mse ~750s, <1200s wall.
